description: Between **1945** and **1975**, more than **80** countries won their independence. The European empires collapsed and the map of the world changed.

hero.hook: In thirty years the colonial empires collapsed and the world map was redrawn.

blocks.text: Between **1945** and **1975**, more than **80 countries** became independent. The European empires, drained by the war, gave way to nationalist movements and to a world far less willing to tolerate colonial rule.
This was not a simple change of flags. It was a global upheaval, right in the middle of the Cold War. It also left behind inherited borders and economic dependence.

The war had shattered the image of invincible mother countries. In **1941** the **[[Atlantic Charter]]**, signed by American president **Franklin D. Roosevelt** and British prime minister **Winston Churchill**, promised peoples the right to choose their own government. Churchill wanted to limit that principle to Europe. African and Asian leaders seized on it for their colonies.

Colonial soldiers had fought for other people's freedom. Elites trained in the West came home with ideas of independence. The United States and the USSR, for opposite reasons, both rejected old-style colonialism. The pressure became impossible to hold back.
Roosevelt had to push Churchill, a defender of the British Empire, before the Atlantic Charter would say anything about the rights of peoples.

Britain often negotiated in order to keep some influence through the **[[Commonwealth]]**, a club of former colonies. India and Pakistan became independent in **1947**. In Ghana, the independence leader **[[Kwame Nkrumah]]** won sovereignty in **1957**, the first British independence in sub-Saharan Africa.

France resisted harder: Indochina until Dien Bien Phu (**1954**), then the Algerian War (**1954-1962**), which brought down the **[[Fourth Republic]]**, the French regime of **1946** to **1958**. In **1960**, the “year of Africa,” **14** French colonies became sovereign. In the Belgian Congo a rushed departure led to chaos and to the murder of **[[Patrice Lumumba]]**, the country's first independent prime minister. Portugal held on until **1975**.

In **1955** the **[[Bandung Conference]]**, held in Indonesia, brought together **29** countries from Asia and Africa. For the first time former colonies spoke with one voice against colonialism and racism. They called for non-alignment: no automatic siding with Washington or Moscow.

The momentum faded fast. Many states slid into a form of **[[Neocolonialism]]**: domination through money, debt or technology rather than through the flag. At the United Nations, though, the South became the majority and forced new subjects onto the agenda: development, apartheid, sovereignty.
The term “Third World” was coined in **1952** by the French demographer **Alfred Sauvy**, by analogy with the Third Estate of **1789**.

blocks.text: Non-alignment took shape at Belgrade in **1961**, around **Josip Broz Tito** of Yugoslavia, **Jawaharlal Nehru** of India and **Gamal Abdel Nasser** of Egypt. But the Cold War pulled many states into one camp or the other. Political independence did not guarantee economic independence.
